title: An evening alone
line: A few hours with no phone and no screen, and what comes up.
intro: It isn’t loneliness we flee, Athena says, but conscience: alone, without distraction, it starts to speak. Athena sees today’s shadows on the wall in the screens we sit before, the news and the feeds; for one evening, switch them off and listen to what comes up instead.
does: Spend one evening of two or three hours alone, with no phone and no screen.
trains: Staying with yourself, and hearing the voice of your conscience.
steps: Choose an evening this week and keep two or three hours of it free. Tell anyone who might need you that you will be offline.
Switch the phone off and put it in another room; leave the television, the laptop and the radio off too. Stay at home, or walk somewhere quiet.
Do nothing in particular: sit, make tea, look out of the window. When something you have pushed down comes up (a worry, a memory, a regret), don’t push it back: let it come, and look at it.
Listen for your conscience: what is it telling you? If it gets heavy, it is enough to have noticed it; you can stop there.
report: What came up, once the screens were off?
What did your conscience say, and what will you do about it?
later: Claude could answer your report in Athena’s terms.
